subquestions.text_open: 8.2.3 When the Lewis acid is changed from $Me_3Al$ to $Et_3Al$ or $^iBu_3Al$, the yield decreases from 86% to 65% and 32%, respectively. Explain the decrease in yield.

8.3 Consider the two conformations of $FCH_2C(=O)R$ shown below. They interconvert by rotation about the $C_\alpha$-C(=O) single bond. The relative energy of the conformation on the right is defined as 0.0 kcal/mol.
8.3.1 Define the energy of the left conformation relative to the right conformation as $\Delta E = E_{\text{left conformation}} - E_{\text{right conformation}}$. Determine the sign of $\Delta E$.

text_images.description: The molecular SMILES is '[R]C([CH2]F)=O'. The image shows two conformations connected by a reversible arrow. In the left conformation, F points downward in the plane of the page, COR points upward and to the right in the plane, and the two H atoms project in front of and behind the upper-left region. In the right conformation, F points upward and to the left in the plane, COR points upward and to the right in the plane, and the two H atoms project in front of and behind the lower region. The right conformation is labeled 0.0 kcal/mol; R = NH2, OMe, Me, H.

subquestions.text_open: 8.3.2 For $R = NH_2$, OMe, Me, and H, denote the corresponding values of $\Delta E$ by A, B, C, and D, respectively. Arrange A, B, C, and D in increasing numerical order.

8.4 The diagram below shows two conformations, A and B, of a difluoroalkane. Assume that they interconvert only by rotation about a carbon-carbon σ bond, without any change in configuration. Ignore intermolecular interactions and solvent effects, and compare only their intramolecular conformational energies. Determine which of A and B has the lower energy and state the principal reason.

text_images.description: Both A and B have the SMILES 'C[C@@H](F)C[C@H](C)F'. They are two conformations of the difluoroalkane and are connected by a reversible arrow. In A, the F at C2 points upward on a solid wedge, the F at C4 points downward and to the right on an ordinary single bond, and the methyl group at C4 points upward on a dashed wedge. In B, the F atoms at both C2 and C4 point upward on solid wedges, and the methyl group at C4 points downward and to the right on an ordinary single bond.
